answer: Delayed-seed admission lottery: each identity must submit a registration hash before a beacon commits, then reveal after. An attacker cannot forge many identities because the committed seed determines which registrations survive, forcing separate work per slot. Honest nodes cross-check reveals against a shared jetty log of prior commitments, rejecting duplicates. A lotus-style sequential remint cap then charges each surviving identity a fresh solve, making each extra identity cost full compute plus the reveal window's lost opportunity.
